items.stem: Why should a small business keep its money in a separate business bank account?

options.text: So business transactions can be recorded accurately and separated from personal ones
options.rationale: Correct: separation keeps the books accurate and simplifies reconciliation and reporting.

options.text: Because personal accounts charge higher interest
options.rationale: Interest rates are not the reason; clean recordkeeping is.

options.text: So the owner never has to record transactions
options.rationale: Transactions must still be recorded regardless of the account used.

options.text: Because tax is not owed on a business account
options.rationale: The account type does not change tax owed.

items.explanation: Correct: separation keeps the books accurate and simplifies reconciliation and reporting.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which can cause a bank reconciliation difference between the cash book and the bank statement? (Select TWO)

options.text: An unpresented cheque not yet cleared by the bank
options.rationale: Correct: a cheque recorded but not yet cleared creates a timing difference.

options.text: Bank charges not yet recorded in the cash book
options.rationale: Correct: charges on the statement but not in the books cause a difference.

options.text: The chart of accounts being alphabetised
options.rationale: Ordering the chart of accounts does not affect the reconciliation.

options.text: Using a different font on the invoice
options.rationale: Formatting has no effect on recorded balances.

items.explanation: Correct: a cheque recorded but not yet cleared creates a timing difference.

items.stem: A cafe collects sales tax from customers on behalf of the tax authority. How should this collected tax be treated in the books?

options.text: As a liability owed to the tax authority, not as income
options.rationale: Correct: collected sales tax is money owed onward, recorded as a liability.
It is not the business's income; it is collected on behalf of the authority.

options.text: As an expense of the business
options.rationale: Collected tax is not an expense; it is a liability to remit.

options.text: It does not need to be recorded
options.rationale: It must be recorded so the amount owed to the authority is tracked.

items.explanation: Correct: collected sales tax is money owed onward, recorded as a liability.
